title: Lack of Control over Registration Data
description: Homeowner may not have control over how their registration data (personal information, device preferences) is stored, shared, or used by third parties after initial enrollment.
assumptions: Assumes data may be shared with service providers or third parties without explicit consent.

title: Incomplete Registration Information
description: Homeowner may not provide complete or accurate information during registration, leading to incomplete device profiles or security vulnerabilities.
assumptions: Assumes homeowner may not fully understand required information or may intentionally omit details.

title: Misleading Data Collection Disclosure
description: Home Hub may not clearly disclose what data is being collected during registration, potentially deceiving homeowner about data practices.
assumptions: Assumes privacy policy or data collection notice may be unclear or not prominently displayed.

title: Unintended Data Usage Consequences
description: Registration data may be used for purposes not disclosed or intended by homeowner, such as targeted advertising or data profiling.
assumptions: Assumes data may be repurposed by service providers or third parties.

title: Access Code Interception
description: The temporary access code entered by the guest user may be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transmission or observation, compromising the confidentiality of the authentication mechanism.

title: Access Code Validation Failure
description: The Home Hub may fail to properly validate the temporary access code, leading to incorrect access decisions or security bypass.

title: Lack of Access Code Audit Trail
description: There is no clear audit trail or verification mechanism to confirm which guest user actually used the access code, making accountability difficult.

title: Impersonation Risk
description: The system may not properly authenticate the guest user, allowing someone to impersonate a legitimate user or use the access code for unauthorized purposes.

title: Unintended Access Consequences
description: The temporary access code may be used for purposes other than unlocking the front door, or the system may be misused for unintended security consequences.

title: Unintended Disclosure of Motion/Door/Sensor Data
description: The local event log may be accessible to unauthorized parties who could access the device's motion/door/sensor data, potentially leading to privacy violations.

title: Lack of Control Over Data Written to Event Log
description: The Home Hub may not have proper controls over what data is written to the local event log, potentially including sensitive information beyond intended scope.

title: Lack of User Notification About Data Logging
description: Users may not be notified about what data is being logged, for how long, or how it will be used, reducing transparency and informed consent.

title: Inadequate Data Retention and Deletion
description: The local event log may not have proper data retention and deletion policies, leading to excessive data accumulation and potential privacy risks.

title: Poor Information Quality in Event Logging
description: The data written to the local event log may be inaccurate, incomplete, or outdated, affecting the reliability of the logged information.

title: Lawfulness of data transfer
description: The transfer of camera clips from Home Hub to Cloud Video Storage may lack a clear legal basis or user consent, potentially violating data protection laws.

title: Notice of data transfer
description: Users may not be adequately informed about the transfer of their recorded video clips to cloud storage, including the purpose, duration, and recipients of the data.

title: Data minimization in transfer
description: The Home Hub may transfer more video data than necessary for the stated purpose, including unnecessary metadata or full-resolution footage.

title: Data accuracy during transfer
description: Video clips may be corrupted, truncated, or altered during the upload process from Home Hub to Cloud Video Storage, affecting their integrity and reliability.

title: Data destruction policy
description: Cloud Video Storage may not have clear policies for data retention and destruction of video clips, leading to indefinite storage of potentially sensitive footage.

title: Unique identification risk
description: Video clips may contain unique identifiers (faces, locations, timestamps) that could be used to uniquely identify individuals, creating profiling risks.

title: Unintended interception of motion alert data during transmission
description: Real-time motion alert data transmitted from Home Hub to Mobile App Backend could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during network transmission, potentially exposing sensitive location and activity information.

title: Insufficient notification of data sharing to users
description: Users may not be adequately informed that their motion alert data is being shared with the Mobile App Backend, violating transparency requirements.

title: Excessive data collection in motion alerts
description: The motion alert data forwarded from Home Hub may include more personal information than necessary for the intended purpose of alerting users to motion events.

title: Unintended access to motion alert data by unauthorized parties
description: Motion alert data stored or processed by the Mobile App Backend could be accessed by unauthorized users or third parties.

title: Inaccurate or delayed motion alert data
description: The Mobile App Backend may receive motion alert data that is inaccurate, incomplete, or delayed, affecting the reliability of the alert system.

title: Disclosure of Home Presence Information
description: Motion-detected notifications may reveal whether someone is present at the homeowner's residence, potentially compromising security and privacy.
assumptions: The notification contains information about motion detection events at the property.

title: Lack of Control Over Notification Timing
description: Homeowner may not have control over when notifications are sent, potentially causing disruption or missing important alerts.
assumptions: The system automatically sends notifications without homeowner intervention.

title: Unintended Use of Motion Data
description: Motion detection data collected for notification purposes may be used for purposes other than the stated purpose of sending alerts.
assumptions: The system may share or use motion data beyond the notification function.

title: Excessive or Inappropriate Notifications
description: Homeowner may receive too many notifications or notifications at inappropriate times, causing privacy intrusion and annoyance.
assumptions: The notification frequency and timing are not customizable by the homeowner.

title: Unintended Disclosure of Aggregated Analytics to Third Parties
description: The cloud analytics vendor (EE3) may share the aggregated device-usage analytics with third parties or resellers without proper user consent or authorization, leading to unintended data disclosure.
assumptions: The analytics vendor operates in a multi-tenant environment and may have business relationships with third parties.

title: Lack of Control Over Data Sharing Scope
description: The mobile app backend (P2) may not have adequate controls to limit the scope of data shared with the analytics vendor, potentially including more data than necessary for analytics purposes.
assumptions: The backend system may lack granular data filtering or consent management capabilities.

title: Non-Compliance with Data Protection Regulations
description: The cloud analytics vendor (EE3) may not comply with applicable data protection regulations (e.g., GDPR, CCPA) regarding the processing and sharing of user analytics data.
assumptions: The analytics vendor operates across multiple jurisdictions with varying data protection requirements.

title: Inaccurate or Misleading Aggregated Data
description: The mobile app backend (P2) may share aggregated device-usage analytics that are inaccurate, incomplete, or misleading, potentially affecting the analytics vendor's reporting and user insights.
assumptions: Data aggregation processes may have errors or biases that affect data quality.

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored Video Data
description: Unauthorized parties may access the video clip during retrieval from cloud storage, potentially through compromised credentials, weak access controls, or insider threats.

title: Video Data Tampering During Storage
description: The stored video clip may be modified or tampered with by malicious actors in the cloud storage system without the homeowner's knowledge.

title: Accidental Video Data Loss During Retrieval
description: The video clip may be accidentally deleted or corrupted during the retrieval process from cloud storage to the mobile app backend.

title: Data Leakage During Video Playback
description: The video clip may be leaked to unauthorized parties during playback on the mobile app, potentially through network interception or app vulnerabilities.

title: Video Quality Degradation Affecting User Experience
description: The retrieved video clip may experience quality degradation during transmission or storage, affecting the user's ability to view the content properly.
